title: Count Numbers with Non-Decreasing Digits
summary: Given two string integers l and r, and an integer b, count the numbers within the range [l, r] (inclusive) that have digits in non-decreasing order when represented in base b.
statement: Given two string integers l and r, and an integer b, count the numbers within the range [l, r] (inclusive) that have digits in non-decreasing order when represented in base b. The result should be modulo 10^9 + 7.
constraints: l and r are decimal strings of up to 100 digits with 1 <= l <= r; 2 <= b <= 10.
A number qualifies when its base-b digits never decrease from left to right.
hints: Counting up to a bound needs only the previous chosen digit, whether a nonzero digit has started, and whether the prefix is tight.
Convert the decimal bound to base b, then use digit DP and subtract counts through l-1 from counts through r.
At each position try digits up to the tight limit, allowing leading zeros or digits at least the previous started digit.
The state captures exactly the prefix restrictions; every qualifying representation follows one path and inclusion-exclusion makes the range inclusive.
editorial: The state captures exactly the prefix restrictions; every qualifying representation follows one path and inclusion-exclusion makes the range inclusive.

tests.explanation: In base eight the range is 27 through 34; only 27, 33, and 34 qualify.
The qualifying binary representations are 11 and 111, giving two.
